comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C33-C40, C96 regarding AMPA/NMDA receptor pharmacology. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic interpretation of the dissociation between BBB modulation (AMPA-dependent) and LTP (both receptors), while peer review accepts this as part of the mechanistic framework without specific critique.

Strong overlap on human fMRI/DCE-MRI data (C67-C70, C76). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledged limitations (small sample, lack of temporal resolution), while peer review rates as UNCERTAIN due to broader concerns about whether the stimulation paradigm truly represents physiological conditions, extending skepticism from rat studies to human experiments.

High overlap on transcriptomic findings (C58-C66). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of DEGs, GO terms, and specific gene categories. Peer review emphasizes the key finding that plasticity genes were implicated but not BBB/inflammation markers, supporting the distinction from pathological conditions.

Both address caveolae-mediated transcytosis via mβCD experiments (C45-C48). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the dissociation between BBB/LTP effects and neurovascular coupling, acknowledging potential non-specific effects. Peer review accepts this as part of the mechanistic evidence without raising concerns.

Both address TGF-β signaling pathway (C52-C57). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the pattern mirroring mβCD results and links to prior literature. Peer review explicitly accepts TGF-β signaling as part of the mechanistic framework linking BBB modulation to plasticity.

Both address justification for 'physiological' stimulation (C103-C107). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the frequency argument and parallels to motor learning. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that while the frequency argument is 'good,' the 2 mA intensity is problematic as it's in a range that can elicit seizures at higher frequencies.

Both address BBB tracer extravasation evidence (C19-C26) and broader claims about physiological nature (C5, C72-C73, C80, C101-C102). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing converging evidence from multiple modalities. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging novelty and strength but maintaining that the explanation for 'physiological' stimulation is 'somewhat weak' due to stimulation intensity concerns.

Both address anesthesia limitations (C109-C111). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the justified choice but acknowledges NMDA antagonism may affect results. Peer review accepts the authors' transparent discussion without raising concerns.

Both address LTP electrophysiology (C27-C29, C43) and related claims (C6, C75). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of electrophysiological and molecular data. Peer review explicitly notes the strength of demonstrating 'long-lasting (>5 hrs)' potentiation without specific critique.

OpenEval R2 includes albumin application experiments (C30-C32) as part of broader LTP evidence. Peer review R3 separately evaluates these albumin experiments as SUPPORTED, acknowledging they demonstrate the mechanistic link between BBB opening and plasticity.

Both address main conclusions synthesizing findings (C3-C4, C71, C77, C116). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate caution about correlative evidence. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, stating 'strength of evidence was convincing' but the persistent weakness in justifying physiological stimulation creates uncertainty about whether this represents normal brain function.

OpenEval R11 includes mβCD limitations (C112-C113) as part of broader limitations discussion, rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R12 separately evaluates mβCD methodology as SUPPORTED, accepting the mitigation strategy without challenge.

Minimal overlap (C81-C82 on TGF-β and transcytosis mechanisms). OpenEval R9 synthesizes findings comparing physiological to pathological conditions (SUPPORTED). Peer review R6 focuses on TGF-β pathway evidence (SUPPORTED). Both accept the mechanistic framework.

Minimal overlap (C99-C100 on transcriptomic summary). OpenEval R15 notes these are redundant summary statements (SUPPORTED). Peer review R7 incorporates these claims into broader transcriptomic evaluation emphasizing distinction from pathological conditions (SUPPORTED).

OpenEval R11 includes sex limitation (C114) in broader limitations discussion (SUPPORTED). Peer review R13 separately notes this as preliminary observation requiring further investigation (SUPPORTED). Both accept this acknowledged limitation.

OpenEval R12 addresses background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C10-C18) establishing scientific foundation, rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are accepted as established knowledge.

OpenEval R13 addresses literature citations supporting mechanistic interpretations (C42, C44, C49-C51, C78-C79, C84-C89, C91-C93, C97-C98), rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background citations are not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R14 addresses speculative mechanisms (C90, C94-C95) rated UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses but not experimentally demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately assess these speculative claims.
